subject: DPA clarifications & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmepayments.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Raj / Marta —

Thanks again for the time on the call this morning. Quick recap + open items so we can keep procurement moving. If helpful I can loop legal (Dev) for any redline-level discussion.

Recap of what we discussed:
- Roles: Acme Payments is the Controller; Redwood would be the Processor for API-hosted inference.
- Subprocessors: you asked for a current subprocessors list and an explanation of notification cadence for changes.
- Breach notice: you asked whether Redwood can commit to breach notification timelines and what we define as a "breach" for the DPA.
- Data residency: any EU residency requirements and options for private deployments / VPC.
- Logging & retention: what logs we retain (access logs, request logs, audit trails), default retention windows, and paid options for extended retention.

Open questions / asks from Acme: (please confirm in-reply)
1) Can Redwood be designated as Processor (we confirmed yes) and accept standard DPA language around processing instructions?
2) Can Redwood provide a list of current subprocessors and commit to a 30-day notice for changes?
3) What is Redwood's standard breach notification SLA (we typically notify within 72 hours) — can you confirm if Acme requires 48 hours and whether that's a hard requirement?
4) Can Redwood support 90-day log retention for audit purposes (note: this is typically a paid add-on for hosted customers)?
5) For PII, please confirm the types of data you expect to send (examples are helpful: cardholder name, last four, full PAN/tokenized data, SSN) so we can ensure appropriate handling.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.4.pdf (our current standard DPA), security_whitepaper.pdf (summary of controls / SOC2 scope).

Next steps:
- Raj / Marta: reply with clarifications on the five items above and attach any redlines to the DPA.
- Marissa: I'll escalate any 48-hour breach requests to legal (Dev) and confirm subprocessors link.
- Aditya: please estimate incremental pricing for extended log retention (90 days) and any hosted vs. private deployment cost delta.
- Target: procurement decision by 2026-07-22 if possible.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v1.4.pdf
Attachment: security_whitepaper.pdf

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmepayments.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick answers and a redline attached:

1) Controller / Processor: confirmed — Acme is Controller; Redwood will be Processor.
2) Subprocessors: please send current list. We also want a commitment for 30 days notice for any new subprocessors.
3) Breach notice: Acme's security policy expects notification within 48 hours of us being made aware of an incident that impacts Acme data. Is Redwood able to commit to 48 hours? If not, please explain the process and escalation path.
4) Log retention: we would prefer 90 days for request/ access logs for compliance. If this is a paid add-on, please provide a ballpark.
5) PII: we'll be sending cardholder name, masked PANs, and email addresses. No full PANs in initial integration, but may request tokens from our PCI provider.

I've attached our DPA redlines (Acme_DPA_redlines_20260712.pdf) — Marta (legal) is copied to review. Please let us know if you need anything else to route this internally.

Regards,
Raj Patel
Head of Platform Security, Acme Payments
raj.patel@acmepayments.com

--
Attachment: Acme_DPA_redlines_20260712.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmepayments.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Raj / Marta —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the redlines. Quick responses inline below and next steps: 

- Subprocessors: current list is published here: https://storage.redwood.example/subprocessors-list-202606.pdf. We provide 30 days' notice for material subprocessor additions; non-material changes are included in quarterly updates. If Acme requires contractual 30-day notice, we can accept that in the DPA.

- Breach notification: our standard commitment is notification within 72 hours for incidents meeting the DPA definition. I understand Acme's preference for 48 hours — I'll escalate this to Dev (legal) to see if we can accommodate 48 hours for conditional cases (severity-based). Dev, can you confirm whether we can accept a 48-hour notification SLA for Acme or propose alternative language (e.g., "commercially reasonable efforts to notify within 48 hours, not to exceed 72 hours")?

- Log retention: hosted customers can add 90-day retention for request/access logs as a paid add-on. Aditya — can you provide an estimate for the hosted plan? Also note: private deployment / dedicated capacity gives customers full control of log retention and residency.

- PII handling: thanks for the details. For cardholder name + masked PANs + emails we are comfortable as long as full PANs are not transmitted. We will ensure encryption in transit and at rest and exclude PCI-sensitive fields from telemetry. If you anticipate tokenization flows that touch full PANs via our runtime, we should flag for SOC/compliance review.

Next steps:
- I'll circulate Acme_DPA_redlines to Legal (Dev) and come back with a proposed redline response by 2026-07-15.
- Aditya to confirm pricing for 90-day retention by 2026-07-13 EOD.
- If Acme is comfortable, we can prepare DocuSign for the DPA + SOW once legal closes the redlines.

Thanks —
Marissa

--
